In Act Two, one character quotes two lines Hamlet speaks to Ophelia after a tramp asks for money. In the third act, a Jewish band plays during a ball where Pischin is astonished by magic tricks. One character in this poem bids the bard Bracy, who has a dream about a bright green snake killing a dove, to leave Langdale Hall with a message for his childhood friend. Donald Keene claims this work's tragedy plays out between its women while the male hero "sits in a stupor." He sees two women knitting black wool before the Company doctor measures his cranium. Beginning with a story describing the beauty of Karintha and a poem about the "Black Reapers" of the title plant, FTP, name this modernist collection of short stories and poems by Jean Toomer.

She wrote about the desire of her childhood friends to rule over "four kingdoms on the sea" in "We Were All to be Queens." Its epigraph is taken from Genesis, and it is dedicated to death of its author's cousin Warren Winslow. The "bones [that] / Cry out… for the hurt beast / Bobbing by Ahab's whaleboats in the East" reside in the title location of, FTP, which poem by Robert Lowell?

Though one himself, his contempt for courtiers is evident in his allegorical criticism of the Star Chamber, "The Bowge of Court." Line 225 describes the birth of Strife and contradicts the opening of another work by its poet, which claims there are two Strifes. The frontispiece of the so-called "phoenix copper" edition of this work features a fantastic creature with a human head, horse's ears, goat's legs, and webbed feet holding a book on which allegorical images are featured, all signifying a satyr, indicating the work's satirical nature. Galway Kinnell ascribed this state to Walt Whitman, calling it a "certain shapelessness of personality, a peculiar power to obliterate himself and flow into some other being and speak it from within." That quality, he wrote in a letter to his brothers on the winter solstice of 1817, is when a man can exist in "uncertainties, mysteries, and doubts, without any irritable reaching after fact and reason," and because of it, for a great poet, "the sense of beauty overcomes every other consideration." One of this man's articles was expanded by computer scientist Charles H. Bennett in 1982, and this man published the short story collection The Voice of the Dolphins. The title character makes Abel Whittle, his eventual caretaker, report to work without pants, and he turns down Joshua Jopp for general manager. Identify this author of the Sentences.

Its characters come "out of all times of trouble, past or future--the great, interrelated family of those who never know the meaning of what has happened to them." Name this novel whose title describes Laurel, a Pulitzer Prize winner by Eudora Welty.

This woman sang over the end credits for the 1990 Dan Akroyd and Gene Hackman film Loose Cannons. During her early career, she sang backup for such diverse acts as Gene Simmons and Bette Midler. One of the title characters reminisces about realizing her husband's infidelity, then carrying on an affair with a groom. Name this Edward Albee play in which the title characters, A, B, and C, realize they love short men, and are in fact the same lady at different ages.

Anachronisms in this work include Cymosco's use of cannons in book four and the presence of Constantine the Great in the last three books. Continued in Lope de Vega's epic poem La Hermosura de Angélica, name this epic in which a French paladin goes on a rampage after losing Angelica, written by Ludovico Ariosto.

The protagonist's son is a sociologist named after the author of "The Culprit Fay," Joseph Rodman Drake. But this novel's protagonist is mostly interested in his grandparents, Susan Burling and Oliver Ward, who were an illustrator and mining engineer, respectively. Name this novel in which a retired history professor writes the biography of his grandmother, a Pulitzer Prize winner by Wallace Stegner.

This work ends with the author comparing his country to an "eagle mewing its mighty youth" and calling it a "nation not slow and dull, but of a quick, ingenious and piercing spirit." What is this poem that, at the author's request, concludes every collection by Alfred Lord Tennyson?

The author drew upon his firsthand exposure to the recovery of a drowned, rigored body for a climactic scene in this novel. Based on its author's experiences at the utopian Brook Farm, name this novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

In Act III, Scene 1 this man severs his own hand thinking to save his sons, but a messenger arrives during the subsequent scene carrying "two heads and a hand." For ten points name the Roman general who revenges himself on Lavinia's attackers by cooking them and serving them to their mother in a pie and is the title character of a notoriously bad Shakespeare play.

His influence can be seen in the work of Lancret and Quillard, and he himself worked with Claude Audran III. Name this French rococo artist, the creator of The Embarkation for Cythera.

A Communist in her early adult years, her penultimate novel, The Diary of a Good Neighbour, was published under the pseudonym Jane Somers. Her first novel was 1950's The Grass is Singing. Her short story collections include The Sun Between Their Feet, but she is better known for her tales of Martha Quest found in Children of Violence, and for another work telling of the writer Anna Wulf and her struggles with the feminist movement. Name this British author of The Golden Notebook.

He referred to his friend Gustave Courbet's painting Stonebreakers as "a condemnation of capitalism and its potential for greed." Name this French socialist and anarchist, author of "What is Property?"

Chapter Two rebukes priests for breaking the Lord's covenant with Levi, along with bashing Judah for marrying "the daughter of a foreign god." Name this Elizabethan drama centering on the nobles of Portugal and a certain other country, written by Thomas Kyd.

At a young age, he recalls having watched old men play pickup baseball games. Name this Jewish patient of Dr. Spielvogel, whose "complaint" is described in Philip Roth's first novel.

The title character of this work leaves Escanes in charge in his absence, during which an attempt by Leonine to kill his daughter is thwarted when the Pirates of Valdes sell her as a prostitute, though she eventually convinces the servant Boult to allow her to teach music. A waiter is duped into kissing Cipolla, who is disguised as Silvestra, and he shoots Cipolla in reprisal. Name the novel that takes place during Stefan's vacation to the Tyrrhenian Sea, by Thomas Mann.

This author's essay "In Praise of Shadows" explores the emerging traditionalism in his best known works. Name this author best known for his depiction of Osaka family life, The Makioka Sisters.

The protagonist of this novel meets his future wife at a dance in England, but the two do not begin a relationship until they sail back to their home country. Name this Chinua Achebe work about the travails of Obi Okonkwo, the sequel to Things Fall Apart.

Their synthesis is blocked by non-steroidal anti-inflammatories like aspirin and naproxen, which work by inhibiting cyclooxygenases. Name these compounds produced by nearly every cell in the body, but which got their name from the Swedish physiologist Ulf von Euler from their discovery in semen.

Minor characters in this work include Bailey, Jake Diefer and Luke Breckinridge. Among the 383 sections of this work are parts entitled "Why We Look Like Epicurians", "The Maxim of the Brute" and "The Egoism of the Stars". The title character nearly wins the hand of the Countess Ida, defeating her suitor, the Chevalier De Magny, at cards. Identify this picaresque novel by William Thackeray.

It contains the story of Esther, who is in love with the preacher King Barlo, whom she catches drunk and in bed with another woman. The final section concerns a man trying to improve the lives of blacks in New York and ends with Father John and Carrie observing a sunrise. Identify this masterpiece of the Harlem Renaissance containing the novella "Kabnis", written by Jean Toomer.

This work's opening section concerns the natural world and includes subsections like "The Birds Arrive" and "The Rivers Come Forth." Other parts include "The Flowers of Punitaqui" and "The Fugitive", though "The Heights of Macchu Picchu" is better known. Identify this collection of 340 poems by Pablo Neruda.

Written while at La Flèche on the Loire River, it was later repudiated as juvenile by its author. It ends with the claim that "When we have found all the meanings and lost all the mysteries, we will be alone, on an empty shore." His plays include Strife and The Silver Box, but he may be better known for novels. But he may be best known for his continuing account of Irene and Soames, collected in Chancery, Awakening, and The Man of Property. FTP, name this British author and creator of The Forsyte Saga.

One of the members of his country's delegation to the International Labor Organization in Geneva, he also served as ambassador to France His short story collections include Burnt Water and Constancia and Other Stories for Virgins. One of his later novels, Terra nostra, describes Philip II's construction of El Escorial, and he wrote a fictionalized account of Ambrose Bierce's last days in The Old Gringo. The winner of the 1987 Cervantes Prize, FTP, name this Mexican author of The Death of Artemio Cruz.

Characteristic works of this school include Evening on the Oise, Cattle at a Watering Place, The Pondant Dagneau, and Early Autumn. At an advanced age, he is reduced to matchmaking, relating the story of Captain Anthony and Flora as proof that "the science of life consists in seizing every chance that presents itself." The solutions to the riddles exchanged in this novel are all symbolic of the person who composed each riddle; the symbols include fireworks, a kite, incense, a mirror, and a pillow. The examination scene in this play is based on the author's use of liquor and bribery to enter the legal bar. Toinette convinces him to fake his death, where he learns that his wife Beline plans to send Angélique to a convent and monopolize his fortune. Name this Molière play centering on the title character Argan, who is a hypochondriac.

This speaker often recalled the childhood sight of Irish patriots' heads paraded through the streets of Cork by British soldiers. Name this co-founder of the Industrial Workers of the World and namesake of a leftist magazine who was still leading strikes in her 90s.

This form was used in Longfellow's translation of the Comedia, and, though the customary division between the proposition and resolution was ignored, it is the form of "On His Being Arrived to the Age of Twenty-three" and "When I Consider How My Light is Spent." Its rules were codified by Guittone of Arezzo, and it was popularized in England by the Earl of Surrey and Thomas Wyatt. It starts new thoughts on the fifth and twelfth lines and resolves itself in a sestet, unlike its later counterpart, which requires a concluding couplet. Identify this specific type of fourteen-line poem named for the admirer of Laura or his country of origin.

Polyeidus advised him to go to the temple of Athena and the well of Peirene, and the stuff he picked up on that journey proved useful in fighting the Solymians, the Amazons, and the Carian pirates. With Philinoe, he was the father of Isander, Laodamia, Hippolochus, and Deidamia. Anteia urged Proetus to have him killed by Iobates, but he acquired a golden bridle and proved undefeatable. Name this son of Eurymede and Glaucus, who slew the Chimera with the aid of Pegasus.

After observing "Dear me, insurrections are becoming tiresome," in the third act of this work, Princess Marghanza sings the "Allegretto a la Seguidilla." The viceroy foils the army by disguising himself as the title figure, then providing copious alcohol and marching the troops to fatigue. This work is set in colonial Peru, where Don Medigua attempts to suppress the rebellion of Cazzaro. At the outbreak of the Spanish-American war, the composer adapted its finale into one of his trademark patriotic marches. Name this operetta by John Phillip Sousa.
